question.worked_solution:
From the identity  ${cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1$ with $\theta =x+\frac{\pi }{6},$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{6})+{sin}^{2}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{6}) & =1 \\ {sin}^{2}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{6})-1 & =-{cos}^{2}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{6}).\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{cos}^{3}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{6})}{{sin}^{2}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{6})-1}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{{cos}^{3}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{6})}{-{cos}^{2}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{6})}\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{6})\,\text{d}x \\  & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+\frac{\pi }{6})+C.\end{aligned}
$$
